why: The old-style copy constructor (the documented old-style constructor shape: an `isa` test on the input, then a copy): `s = varargin{1}` after an `isa` test is the object, and `class(struct(…), 'Bolt')` makes one, so `tidy(s)` is `Bolt::tidy` on both paths (step 15 round 7: of the method's own object only a write whose value is clearly something else ends the hint, and `varargin{…}` is not one).
